Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 105 s. 2022 September 28, 2022 HON. SOL F. MATUGAS Mayor Municipality of General Luna, Province of Surigao del Norte Dear Mayor Matugas: This has reference to your letter dated 15 August 2022 regarding your request for legal opinion on the propriety and validity of Executive order (EO) No. 004, s. 2022 issued by Gov. Robert Lyndon S. Barbers, Province of Surigao del Norte, alleging that it is in conflict with Provincial Ordinance No. 05 s. of 2022. In your letter, you stated therein that more than eight (8) years ago, during his term as the Provincial Governor of the Province of Surigao del Norte, a building owned by the Provincial Government of Siargao named "Kapitolyo Nan Siargao" (KNS) was contstructed in the Municipality of Dapa, Surigao del Norte which served as the extension offices of the Provincial Governor, Provincial Vice Governor, Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Provincial Assessor, Provincial Social Welfare and Development, and other provincial departments, wherein it already became historic. Then on 06 June 2022, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Surigao del Norte passed Provincial Ordinance No. 05 s. 2022, entitled "An Ordinance Officially Declaring the Kapitolyo Nan Siargao' in the Municipality of Dapa, Surigao del Norte as the Extension or Sub-Offices of the Provincial Govemor, Provincial Vice Govemor, Sangguniang Panlalawigan, Provincial Assessor, Provincial Social Welfare and Development, and Such Other Provincial Departments". Meanwhile, on 12 July 2022, Gov. Robert Lyndon S. Barbers, Province of Surigao del Norte, issued Executive order (EO) No. 004, s. 2022 declaring "Kapitolyo Nan Siargao" to be known as the "GOVERNOR EXTENSION OFFICE OF SIARGAO". Under this premise arose the request for assistance and clarification regarding the following issues: I. Whether a Provincial Ordinance can be validly amended by a mere Executive Order of the Provincial Governor?; 2. Whether Gov. Robert Lyndon S. Barbers has encroached on the power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Surigao del Norte provided under Section 13(A)(5) of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", as amended (LGC), in relation to renaming public building, in consultation with the Philippine Historical Commission, owned by the provincial government, when he issued EO No. 004, s. 2022?; "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

3. Whether Gov. Robert Lyndon S. Barbers violated Section 465(B)(2) of the LGC when he issued EO No. 004, s. 2022 instead of enforcing Provincial Ordinance No. 05 s. 2022? At the outset, we would like to establish that while this Department exercises general supervision over local government units (LGUs), we have no authority to declare invalid any executive order issued by the local chief executives, or ordinances and resolutions of the local sanggunians, or any act committed by the members thereof which is alleged to be in violation of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) or other applicable laws. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of the appropriate action for Declaratory Relief before the proper court, in accordance with Section I, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court. Moreover, the Department is proscribed to act on queries regarding presumptively valid acts, e.g., enacted ordinances, consummated acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, and similar cases. For this reason, we shall discuss only the provisions of law or rules which we deem applicable based on the representations in the letter. To begin with, considering that all the queries pertain to the same matter, we deem it proper to address them in one discussion. In reply thereto, may we invite your attention to the following provisions of the LGC in relation to local legislative power: "SECTION 48. Local Legislative Power. — Local legislative power shall be exercised bv the sanqqunianq panlalawiqan for the province; the sangguniang panlungsod for the city; the sangguniang bayan for the municipality; and the sangguniang barangay for the barangay. " xxx xxx xxx "SECTION 468. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. — (a) The sangguniang panlalawigan, as the legislative body of the province, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the province and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the province as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: xxxx " Correspondingly, the LGC explicitly provides that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, having the local legislative power, has the authority to determine which acts are necessary for an efficient and effective municipal government for the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants. It is settled that ordinances enacted by our local sanggunians have the force and effect of law within the jurisdiction of the local government unit enacting it. Accordingly, since it is an ordinance, it may be amended or repealed only by another ordinance, enacted with the same formalities as the ordinance being amended or repealed. Page 2 of 3

While the Provincial Governor is empowered under the LGC to issue executive orders for the faithful and appropriate enforcement and execution of laws and ordinances, it cannot amend an enacted ordinance since amendment of an ordinance is essentially an exercise of legislative power which belongs to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. To do so is tantamount to an encroachment by the Provincial Governor on the power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Further, as stated above, an ordinance can only be amended by another ordinance. In this regard, we would like to highlight Section 13(a)(5) of the LGC which specifically states that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan may, in consultation with the Philippine Historical Commission (PHC), change the name of any their public place or building owned by the provincial government within its territorial jurisdiction. Lastly, it may be worthy to remind that under Section 465 (b)(2) of the LGC, the provincial governor is mandated to enforce all laws and ordinances within the province and for this, in subparagraph (iii) thereof, he shall issue such executive orders for the faithful and appropriate enforcement and execution of laws and ordinances. Let it be noted that such duty of the provincial governor to enforce and implement all laws and ordinances shall be regardless of his belief. Should the provincial governor believes that the previously enacted ordinance suffers from legal remedy, his remedy is not to issue an executive order amending or modifying the ordinance. Rather, he must question the ordinance to the proper court and ask for a restraining order so that in the meantime, he can be legally justified in not implementing the ordinance. Notwithstanding, we would like to stress that this opinion is being issued without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A Un J ANVI TOR R.
